meta.note: Evidence records support editorial freshness dates. They do not replace the linked authority or a traveller's passport-specific confirmation.

reviews.evidence: SAPS confirms 10111 for police emergencies; South African government guidance confirms 10177 for ambulance and 112 for mobile emergencies.
NamPol confirms the countrywide police emergency line 10111. City of Windhoek confirms 061 211111 for ambulance, fire and rescue within the municipal boundary.
Botswana Police confirms 999; the Government of Botswana emergency medical service confirms ambulance 997. The police emergency directory also lists fire 998.
Zambia Police lists emergency 991, ambulance 992 and fire 993. The previous police number 999 was removed.
Zimbabwe's Ministry of Health Impilo service lists 999 for ambulance, police and fire, with 112 as the alternative emergency number. The previous service-specific numbers were removed.
Mozambique's official tourism information lists 112 and 122 for police/emergency contact. The previous 119/117 summary was removed.
Malawi's Ministry of Homeland Security lists police 997, fire 998 and ambulance 999. The previous summary incorrectly labelled 998 as ambulance.
The Government of Lesotho lists national emergency 112 and national ambulance 121. The unsubstantiated police number 123 was removed.
The Government of Eswatini lists police 999 and fire 933; its health emergency service confirms ambulance 977.
DHA guidance makes eligibility passport-specific and provides an ETA route for eligible travellers. Broad regional promises were replaced with a passport-dependent summary.

Namibia's official visa-on-arrival service and government fact sheet confirm the reciprocal regime introduced on 1 April 2025, including the N$1,600 standard adult fee for affected non-African passports.
Government guidance confirms nationality-based exemptions, six-month passport validity and a maximum 90-day visitor stay in a calendar year.
Zambia Immigration confirms three nationality categories, a visitor/tourist allowance up to 90 days in 12 months, and the USD 50 KAZA UniVisa for eligible trips.
Zimbabwe Immigration confirms the A/B/C regime: visa-free, visa obtainable at port of entry, and prior eVisa respectively. The previous summary did not distinguish these categories.

Zimbabwe's current regime shows the selected UK, US, Australian, Canadian and Indian profiles as visa-required but eligible at the port of entry; the EU grouping requires nationality-specific checking. Incorrect visa-free claims were removed.
Mozambique's new official portal distinguishes regional exemptions, a 30-day eTA list, the broader eVisa scheme and embassy-only passports. The former generic visa-on-arrival claim was removed.
The official eligibility table confirms 30-day eTA eligibility for UK, US and Canadian passports, eVisa eligibility for Australia and India, and 30-day exemption for ordinary South African passports.

Malawi's 2026 amendment requires visas except for the current exemption schedule. A notice effective 24 February 2026 allows Category Two nationals to use visa on arrival while Category One needs approval before departure; eVisa is recommended for eligible travellers.

The 2026 exemption schedule removed the former broad exemption for UK, US, EU, Australian and Canadian ordinary passports. The matrix now marks a visa action and sends travellers to the official eligibility wizard instead of promising visa on arrival across all profiles.
Lesotho Home Affairs says foreign visitors generally need the eVisa unless covered by a visa-abolition agreement or an eligible Commonwealth exemption.
Eswatini's official guidelines make the requirement nationality-specific and limit the visitor visa category to stays of no more than one month.
